Name: Aluminium
Fireworks usage: Aluminium metal is used to produce silver and white flames and sparks. It is a common component of sparklers.

Name: Barium
Fireworks usage: Barium salts are used to create green colors in fireworks, and it can also help stabilize other volatile elements.

Name: Carbon
Fireworks usage: Carbon is one of the main components of black powder, which is used as a propellent in fireworks. Carbon provides the fuel for a firework. Common forms include carbon black, sugar, or starch.

Name: Chlorine
Fireworks usage: Chlorate and perchlorates are common oxidizers.

Name: Iron
Fireworks usage: Iron powder is used to produce sparks in sparklers.

Name: Potassium
Fireworks usage: Potassium nitrate, potassium chlorate, and potassium perchlorate are common oxidizers. The potassium content imparts a faint violet color to the sparks.

Name: Magnesium
Fireworks usage: Magnesium metal burns a very bright white, so it is used to add white sparks or improve the overall brilliance of a firework.

Name: Sodium
Fireworks usage: Sodium imparts a gold or yellow color to fireworks, however, the color is often so bright that it frequently masks other, less intense colors. Sodium lamps operate with the same optical emission.

Name: Oxygen
Fireworks usage: Oxygen is a component of chlorate and perchlorate, common oxidizers.

Name: Sulfur
Fireworks usage: Sulfur is a component of black powder, and as such, it is found in a propellant/fuel.

Name: Strontium
Fireworks usage: Strontium salts impart a red color.

Name: Titanium
Fireworks usage: Titanium metal can be burned as powder or flakes to produce silver sparks.

Name: Zirconium
Fireworks usage: Zirconium, like titanium, burns to produce oxides that emit brightly. It is used in waterfalls.
